chunks: ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from al-Sayyārī, from Muḥammad ibn Jumhūr, from some of our companions, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

Indeed, Fāṭimah bint Asad, the mother of Amīr al-Muʾminīn, was the first woman to emigrate to Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله from Makkah to al-Madīnah on her own feet, and she was among the most dutiful of people toward Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله.

She heard Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله while he was saying: “The people will be raised on the Day of Resurrection naked, just as they were born.” So she said, “Oh, what shame!” Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله said to her, “Then I ask Allah to raise you clothed.” And she heard him mention the pressure of the grave, so she said, “Oh, what weakness!” Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله said to her, “Then I ask Allah to spare you that.” And one day she said to Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله, “I wish to free this servant-girl of mine.” He said to her, “If you do so, Allah will free with each limb of hers a limb of yours from the Fire.”

When she fell ill, she made a bequest to Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله and instructed that her servant be freed. Her tongue became unable to speak, so she began gesturing to Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله, and Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله accepted her bequest. Then one day while he was seated, Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام came to him weeping. Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله said to him, “What makes you weep?” He said, “My mother Fāṭimah has died.” Rasūl Allāh said, “And by Allah, she was my mother as well,” and he rose quickly and went in.

He looked at her and wept. Then he instructed the women to wash her and said, “When you have finished, do not do anything further until you inform me.” When they finished, they informed him of that, so he gave them one of his shirts, the one that touched his body, and instructed them to shroud her in it. And he said to the Muslims, “When you see me do something that I have not done before, then ask me why I did it.”

When they had finished washing her and shrouding her, he صلى الله عليه وآله came in and carried her bier upon his shoulder. He remained beneath her bier until he brought her to her grave. Then he placed her down, entered the grave, and lay in it. Then he took her in his hands until he placed her in the grave. Then he bent over her for a long time, speaking confidentially to her, and saying to her: “Your son, your son, your son.”

Then he came out and leveled the soil over her. Then he bent over her grave, and they heard him saying: “There is no god but Allah. O Allah, I entrust her to You.” Then he departed. The Muslims said to him, “We saw you do things today that you had not done before.” He said, “Today I lost the devoted care of Abū Ṭālib. Whenever she had something with her, she would prefer me with it over herself and her children. I had mentioned the Resurrection and that people would be raised naked, so she said, ‘Oh, what shame!’ and I guaranteed to her that Allah would raise her clothed. I mentioned the pressure of the grave, so she said, ‘Oh, what weakness!’ and I guaranteed to her that Allah would spare her that. So I shrouded her in my shirt, and I lay down in her grave for that reason, and I bent over her and instructed her with what she would be asked about. She was asked about her Lord, and she spoke; she was asked about her Messenger, and she answered; and she was asked about her guardian and her Imam, so she became shaken over it, and I said: ‘Your son, your son, your son.’”

key_terms.إِمَامِهَا: her Imam, the one whose leadership she is asked about
key_terms.الْقِيَامَةِ: the Day of Resurrection when people are raised for judgment
key_terms.جَنَازَتَهَا: her funeral bier or body being carried for burial
key_terms.ضَغْطَةَ الْقَبْرِ: the pressure or constriction of the grave after burial
key_terms.كَاسِيَةً: clothed, referring to being raised covered on the Day of Judgment
key_terms.وَلِيِّهَا: her guardian, referring here to the divinely designated authority

ai.seo_question: Why did Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله shroud Fāṭimah bint Asad in his shirt and lie in her grave?
ai.summary: This narration describes the virtues of Fāṭimah bint Asad and the special care Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله showed her at her death and burial. It emphasizes her devotion, the realities of resurrection and the grave, and the importance of being prepared to answer about one’s Lord, Messenger, and Imam.
